Smaller project · Max Planck Institute · 2026

A social media kit students can post with

The XPLO judo study at a Max Planck Institute researches cognitive control in sport. Its Instagram account is run by student assistants. I built them a small Figma kit, so every post looks like Max Planck without anyone having to be a designer.

Role
Brand and visual design, end to end: look and feel, foundations, templates
Channel
Instagram @mpi.judo
Tools
Figma (variables, components), Gemini as sparring partner
Scope
14 colors, 2 fonts, 8 type styles, spacing, border and radius scale, 5 components, post and story templates, moodboard

Problem

Students posted without rules for a feed

The student assistants change often and have no design background. The Max Planck CI covers print and web, but has no rules for a feed. Posts mixed styles and were heavy on text, and they showed neither the research nor the judo.

Hypothesis. If student assistants get a small, ready-made kit (tokens with usage rules built in, plus a few templates), they can build an on-brand post in under 30 minutes, without deciding colors, type or spacing themselves.

The approach

Started from the Max Planck green

Started with a moodboard. "Neugier in Bewegung" puts track and lab side by side: motion photos, lab scenes, microscopy, force curves and tape collage.

Kept the Max Planck greens as the base. MPG Green and MPG Green Dark come straight from the CI and carry the research side.

Added orange and mint as accents. Performance Orange is the warm complement to the cool green. Electric Mint works as a highlight on dark green. Both stay at about 10 % of a post: hooks, key numbers, CTAs.

Extended the palette to 14 tones. Four groups: Primary, Base & Text, Accent & Sport, Data & Function. Light tints like Mint Tint keep text boxes readable, data colors separate curves in charts.

Gave research and sport their own background. Off-White for research and longer explanations, dark green for sport and hooks. Alternating them breaks up the feed.

Foundations

Wrote the rules into Figma

Kept the MPG house fonts. Merriweather carries hooks and quotes, Roboto carries data, tags and CTAs. Both are official MPG fonts, so the kit stays within the CI.

Limited each scale to three steps. Spacing 8 / 16 / 24 px, borders 1 / 2 / 4 px, radius 0 / 8 px / pill.

Wrote usage rules into the semantic tokens. The description shows up as a tooltip in Figma when someone picks a color, e.g. Mint Tint is only for local highlights.

Marked every chart as illustrative. The study has no results yet, so the templates make no clinical claims.

Result

Every post now starts from one design guide

The team gets a moodboard, the foundations, 5 components and templates for a feed post (4:5) and 2 story layouts (9:16), each with a filled example.

Result

Waiting for data.

What I took away

What I learned

  • Fewer tokens, more rulesSocial media needed fewer tokens than a product. The rules work best inside Figma, at the moment someone picks a color.
  • Type scales differently on socialOn a 1080 px canvas, hooks run at 126 px and body text at 36 px.
  • A kit leaves room to createEvery post stays recognizable as Max Planck, while the students still choose the topic, the image and the story.
